We need to propose a retrosynthesis route for target SMILES: O=S(NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O

We must use templates in order: ['20810', '2895', '1914397', '1914398', '1914399', '74054'] and have at least 6 reactions. So exactly 6 steps using each template sequentially.

We have already applied 20810 to target, got two fragments: (1) CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1 and (2) O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F

So first reaction splits target into those two precursors.

Now we need to apply template 2895 to one of those fragments (presumably the first). We applied 2895 to that fragment, got product: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1 (i.e., nitro substitution). So second reaction transforms the aromatic amine to nitro.

Third template 1914397: we tried applying to O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F but got no result. Also applied to the nitro aromatic fragment gave two fragments: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCNCC1 and O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2 . So third reaction splits that fragment into a protected amine (tert-butyl carbamate?) and a brominated aromatic fused ring.

Now fourth template 1914398 applied to the brominated fused ring gave BrBr and O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2 . So it removes bromine? Actually splits off BrBr (bromine molecule) and leaves the rest.

Fifth template 1914399 applied to ??? We haven't applied yet. Likely to the O=[N+]... fragment to open ring? Let's try applying 1914399 to O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2 .
